question: proofgate is a text gate on the Bash command, so a proof run from a script FILE (bash run_it.sh, whose text names no proof) can never be seen by it; measured 2026-11-13 it runs bare and writes into HOME/.cairn. Which physics should seal that spelling: (a) every proof refuses to run unless it is inside the tester's seal (one check in a shared helper or at the scratch door), (b) the hook also reads the script file a bash/sh command names, or (c) the script-file hand is accepted as outside the rule?
why_it_blocks: dda0e72b9c67 clause 4 is red on two spellings: xargs (decidable in the gate) and a script file (not visible to any text gate); the fix for the second is a design choice that reopens 72a37498c601's WRONG INTENT clause.
answer: CC's decision (Akien 2026-11-17: the gates exist so the build delivers what the ticket says; this is CC's to adjudicate): (a). Ticket dda0e72b9c67's outcome is that no proof run writes live ~/.cairn, so the tooth measures that outcome — a proof refuses to run outside the tester's seal — not the spelling of the command. proofgate stays a convenience that rewrites the common spelling; it is no longer the seal, and clause 4 stops enumerating spellings.
